entities.evidence: This verse closes the lifespan of Enoch’s son Methuselah, introduced in Genesis 5:21 and named as Lamech’s father in Genesis 5:25. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with יְמֵי in כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “all the days of Methuselah.” The following numeral phrase gives the total length of his life, 969 years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.
analysis.sense: to be (of a quantity or duration), to amount to

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח means “all the days of Methuselah.” The verse gives their sum as 969 years, so כָּל refers to his entire lifespan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח, the construct form יְמֵי links the days to Methuselah. The verse totals them as 969 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died,” identifying them as his full lifespan.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “all the days of Methuselah,” the name identifies whose lifespan is counted. The verse gives his age as 969 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In תֵּשַׁע וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, “sixty-nine years,” the marked תֵּשַׁע supplies the nine units and וְשִׁשִּׁים supplies the sixty. The feminine form counts שָׁנָה, “year.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: nine as the units component of sixty-nine

analysis.evidence: In תֵּשַׁע וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, “nine and sixty years,” the marked word contributes sixty to Methuselah’s lifespan of 969 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, plural absolute, common to both genders.

analysis.evidence: In תֵּשַׁע וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, the singular noun supplies the unit for sixty-nine. These years and the following nine hundred make up כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “all the days of Methuselah,” giving his lifespan as 969 years.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clarify the Genesis 5:27 evidence under nine-compounds by identifying the second occurrence of the numeral and the noun it counts.
draft.definition: The cardinal number nine. Before מֵאוֹת it specifies nine hundreds.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:27 uses וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה for the nine hundred years in Methuselah’s total.

analysis.evidence: In וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the marked numeral counts מֵאוֹת, “hundreds.” The conjunction adds these nine hundred years to the preceding sixty-nine years, giving Methuselah a lifespan of 969 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ prefixed to תְשַׁע, the feminine singular construct form of the cardinal numeral.
analysis.sense: Nine as the multiplier of a hundred.

analysis.evidence: In וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, תְּשַׁע counts nine hundreds, giving nine hundred years. The preceding sixty-nine years bring Methuselah’s lifespan to 969 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for “nine hundred years.” Added to the preceding sixty-nine years, it gives the total for כָּל יְמֵי מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “all the days of Methuselah,” before וַיָּמֹת, “and he died.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After totaling Methuselah’s lifespan at 969 years, the verse closes with וַיָּמֹת. Methuselah is the singular subject, and the verb records his death.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life
